tools.name: projects
tools.title: List your projects
tools.description: Your projects, most recently touched first: id, name, the start of its brief, whether it carries a look, and how many scenes it holds (and how many are rendered). `include_archived` adds the archived ones. Returns at most `limit` rows (default 25, maximum 100). Read-only.

include_archived.title: Include Archived

limit.description: How many projects to return, 1 to 100.
limit.title: Limit

tools.name: project
tools.title: Open one project
tools.description: One project in full, by its id from `projects`: its brief and look, what it learned from the scenes rendered and edited in it, its scenes (status, the start of each scene prompt, its still or clip), the reference images those scenes used, the renders made for it, and the latest turns of its chat in the studio. Up to 50 scenes and 60 references, newest scenes first; `chat_turns` sets how many turns (default 12, maximum 40); page further back with `project_chat`. Read-only.

chat_turns.description: How many of the latest chat turns to include, 0 to 40.

tools.title: Read a project's chat history

Returns the newest `limit` turns (default 40, maximum 200, and fewer when the turns are long); pass `before` (the oldest turn id you already hold) to page further back; `has_more` says whether older turns exist. Read-only.

before.description: A turn id you already hold: only older turns are returned, to page back. Omit for the newest.
before.title: Before

limit.description: How many turns to return, 1 to 200.
limit.title: Limit

tools.name: create_project
tools.title: Create a project
tools.description: Start a new project: a name, an optional brief (who it is for, what it must always have and never show) and an optional look (the style every scene in it is held to). It appears on your projects board in the studio, and `write_scene` with its `project_id` files a scene under it. Spends nothing.

brief.description: Who the work is for, and what it must always have and never show. Optional.
brief.title: Brief

look.description: The visual style every scene in the project is held to. Optional.
look.title: Look

tools.name: elements
tools.title: List your elements
tools.description: Your elements: the characters, props and places whose photos you uploaded in the studio or added with `add_element`, each with its photo refs. Pass a photo's `ref` wherever a tool asks for one of your photos (a scene's refs, or a reference for a render or an effect); refs from this list are the only ones taken. Read-only.

annotations.title: List your elements

tools.name: add_element
tools.title: Add a picture as an element (no credits)
tools.description: Add ONE picture to your elements -- the characters, props and places a scene is held to. `kind` is character, prop or location; `name` is what to call it, and a name you already have of that kind gains the picture instead of making a second element; `notes` says what it is in a few words. `source` is the picture: the https address the person gave you (never one you guessed) of an image file (jpg, png or webp, up to 15 MB) or of a product's page -- from a page its main product picture is taken, and what the page states about the product (name, brand, colour, size) is kept in the notes as text copied off the page, or `gen:<id>`, an image `project` lists among a project's renders. Returns the element with its photo `ref`s, as `elements` lists them. Nothing is drawn and no credits are spent: the picture is saved as it is and described in words for the studio.

kind.description: What the element is: character, prop or location.
kind.title: Kind

name.description: What to call the element; a name you already have of that kind gains this picture instead of making a second element.
name.title: Name

source.description: The picture: an https address the person gave you (an image file or a product page), or an image's id such as `gen:<id>`.
source.title: Source

notes.description: What it is, in a few words. Optional.
notes.title: Notes

annotations.title: Add a picture as an element (no credits)

tools.name: upload_link
tools.title: Get a one-time page for the person to upload a file (no credits)
tools.description: A one-time web page where the person uploads ONE file from their phone or computer into their studio -- the way in for a picture or a clip that is not already at a web address. `purpose` is reference (a picture to hold a scene to) or footage (a clip, or a still, for the editor). With `element_kind` (character, prop or location) and `element_name`, the picture is also added to that element, so `elements` lists it afterwards and a scene can be held to it. Give the person the `url` and tell them to open it, pick the file and come back; the page takes jpg, png, webp or heic pictures and mp4 or mov clips, checked by their contents, and shows the file's id when it is saved. A link is good for thirty minutes and for one file: for another file, call this again. Spends nothing and draws nothing.

purpose.description: reference (a picture to hold a scene to) or footage (a clip, or a still, for the editor).
purpose.title: Purpose

element_kind.description: character, prop or location: the uploaded picture is also added to that element. Optional.
element_kind.title: Element Kind

annotations.title: Get a one-time page for the person to upload a file (no credits)

tools.name: video_models
tools.title: List the video models
tools.description: The video models a scene can be rendered on: id, the lengths in seconds and the frames (resolutions) each takes, the credits a short clip costs at each frame, and the cheaper draft frame where a model has one. `quote` prices a scene exactly. Read-only; spends nothing.

annotations.title: List the video models

tools.name: write_scene
tools.title: Save a scene you wrote
tools.description: Save a scene prompt you wrote with the person as a scene, ready to render in the studio. `prompt` is the full scene (an opening line naming the attached photos, a style block, timed beats like (0-4s) each one shot, diegetic sound, an avoid list); `seconds` is its total length (4-30); `refs` are photo refs from `elements` -- the first one anchors the render. A scene needs at least one before it can be priced or rendered: with none it is saved as a draft, and you add a photo (`add_element`) and call this again with its `scene_id` and `refs`. Timed beats become the shots. `roles` says what a photo is FOR when it is not its subject -- {ref: role}, a role being subject, product, place, light, palette, framing or style; a look-only photo is never the anchor. `title` names it (a few words). `project_id` (from `projects`) files it in that project. Pass `scene_id` to rewrite a scene you saved before. Returns the scene's id and its studio link. Spends nothing.

prompt.description: The full scene prompt, with timed beats like (0-4s), each one shot.
prompt.title: Prompt

seconds.description: The scene's total length in seconds, 4 to 30. Optional.
seconds.title: Seconds

refs.description: Photo refs from `elements` the scene is held to; the first one anchors the render.
refs.title: Refs

title.description: A short name for the scene. Optional.
title.title: Title

project_id.description: A project id from `projects` to file the scene in. Optional.
project_id.title: Project Id

scene_id.description: A scene you saved before, to rewrite it instead of making a new one. Optional.
scene_id.title: Scene Id

roles.description: What a photo is for when it is not the scene's subject: {ref: role}, the role one of subject, product, place, light, palette, framing or style. Optional.
roles.title: Roles

annotations.title: Save a scene you wrote

tools.name: scene
tools.title: Read one scene and its renders
tools.description: One of your scenes by its `scene_id` (from `write_scene` or `project`): its title, project, the scene prompt and timed shots, how many reference photos it renders against, where it stands, the clips rendered so far and a link to open it in the studio. Use it to check whether a render has landed. Read-only.

annotations.title: Read one scene and its renders

tools.name: quote
tools.title: Price the keyframes and the clip
tools.description: What rendering one of your scenes (`scene_id`, from `write_scene` or `project`) would cost in the studio, in credits -- the keyframe stills still to draw and the clip, one render per timed shot -- beside your balance, and `approve_url`, the scene's page in the studio where the person approves the render. Nothing here renders or spends. Optional `provider`, `model`, `duration` (whole-scene only) and `frame` price a different renderer. Read-only.

provider.description: The renderer. Omit for the studio's default.
provider.title: Provider

model.description: A video model id from `video_models`. Omit for the default.
model.title: Model

duration.description: The clip's length in seconds for a scene rendered whole. Omit to use the scene's.
duration.title: Duration

frame.description: The resolution, e.g. 720p, one the model takes. Omit for the default.
frame.title: Frame

annotations.title: Price the keyframes and the clip

tools.name: job
tools.title: Check a background job
tools.description: The status of a background job by id -- a render or a free edit this connector started, or one you started in the studio: status, label, progress detail and the result or error when it finished. `wait` (0 to 15 seconds) holds the answer until the job finishes or that long has passed, so a short job is read in one call. Jobs live in memory, so a server restart forgets them; a render still lands on its scene, so read `scene` if a job is gone. Read-only.

job_id.description: The job's id, from the tool that started it.
job_id.title: Job Id

wait.description: Seconds to wait for the job to finish before answering, 0 to 15.
wait.title: Wait

annotations.title: Check a background job

tools.name: library
tools.title: List what is in your library (renders and uploads)
tools.description: What is in your studio's library, newest first: your renders (`gen:<id>`) and the files you brought in (`asset:<id>`, through `upload_link` or the studio's editor), each with its kind (image, video or audio), length, size, frame and the project it belongs to. `kind` narrows to image, video, audio, upload (files you brought in) or render; `project_id` (from `projects`) to one project. These ids are what `share_link`, `reformat`, `trim_clip`, `assemble_clips` and `add_element` take. Returns at most `limit` rows (default 20, maximum 100). Read-only.

kind.description: Narrow to image, video, audio, upload (files you brought in) or render. Omit for everything.
kind.title: Kind

limit.description: How many items to return, 1 to 100.
limit.title: Limit

project_id.description: Only this project's items (an id from `projects`). Optional.
project_id.title: Project Id

annotations.title: List what is in your library (renders and uploads)

tools.name: share_link
tools.title: Get a download link for one of your files
tools.description: A link that downloads one of your renders or uploads (`ref`: a `gen:<id>` or `asset:<id>` from `library`), good for `hours` (default 24, at most 168 -- seven days). Anyone holding the link can download the file until it expires, so hand it to the person, never to a page. Each call makes a new link; the file itself is unchanged and nothing is spent.

ref.description: One of your files by id: a `gen:<id>` or `asset:<id>` from `library`.

hours.description: How long the link works, 1 to 168 hours.

tools.name: reformat
tools.title: Make a copy of a clip or still in a new shape (no credits)
tools.description: A copy of one of your clips or stills in a new shape. `ref` is a `gen:<id>` or `asset:<id>` from `library`; `aspect` is 9:16, 16:9, 1:1 or 4:5; `fit` is pad (the whole picture, black where the shapes differ -- the default) or crop (the picture fills the frame, the middle kept; refused when the two shapes are too far apart). The source is untouched; the result is a new item in your library and an editable cut in the studio's editor. It runs on the studio's own server, so it spends no credits, and runs in the background: poll `job`.

ref.description: One of your files by id: a `gen:<id>` or `asset:<id>` from `library`.
ref.title: Ref

fit.description: pad (the whole picture, black where the shapes differ) or crop (the picture fills the frame).
fit.title: Fit

title.description: A short name for the result, a few words. Optional.
title.title: Title

tools.title: Make a new clip from a range of one of yours (no credits)
tools.description: A new clip holding `start` to `end` seconds of one of your clips (`ref`: a `gen:<id>` or `asset:<id>` from `library`), with the clip's own sound. The range must lie inside the clip. The source is untouched; the result is a new item in your library. Spends no credits (it runs on the studio's own server) and runs in the background: poll `job`.

ref.description: One of your files by id: a `gen:<id>` or `asset:<id>` from `library`.
ref.title: Ref

start.description: Where the new clip starts, in seconds.
start.title: Start

end.description: Where the new clip ends, in seconds.
end.title: End

title.description: A short name for the result, a few words. Optional.
title.title: Title

project_id.description: A project id from `projects`: the result is filed under that project. Optional.
project_id.title: Project Id

tools.name: assemble_clips
tools.title: Join clips into one video (no credits)
tools.description: Join clips from your library into ONE video, in the order given: `clips` are two to twenty `gen:<id>` or `asset:<id>` videos from `library` (the same id may repeat). `transition` is cut (the default) or crossfade (`crossfade_s`, 0.1-2 seconds, at most half the shortest clip). `music` is an optional bed under the clips' own sound -- an `asset:<id>` audio file from `library` (kind=audio), trimmed to the picture and lowered under the clips' sound. Clips of different shapes (9:16 beside 16:9) are refused unless `letterbox` is true, which fits them inside the first clip's frame with black bars. `project_id` (from `projects`) files the result under that project. Spends no credits: it runs on the studio's own server. Runs in the background: poll `job`; the result is a new `gen:<id>` in your library and an editable cut in the studio's editor.

clips.description: Two to twenty videos by id, in the order they play.
clips.title: Clips

crossfade_s.description: The crossfade's length in seconds, 0.1 to 2.
crossfade_s.title: Crossfade S

music.description: An audio file's `asset:<id>` to lay under the clips. Optional.
music.title: Music

letterbox.description: true to fit clips of different shapes inside the first clip's frame with black bars.
letterbox.title: Letterbox

title.description: A short name for the result, a few words. Optional.
title.title: Title

project_id.description: A project id from `projects`: the result is filed under that project. Optional.
project_id.title: Project Id

annotations.title: Join clips into one video (no credits)
